label: agenda.statechart
lead: A computer cannot be punished, and it does not need to be. What makes a system accountable in practice is a set of mechanisms: we know what it was allowed to do, which component did what and from which evidence, and how to contain and repair a mistake. My research engineers these mechanisms for AI agents with model-driven engineering, so that the people responsible for agentic systems can actually exercise that responsibility.
reading: Read it clockwise: a person delegates work under a contract (①); agents report back with evidence (②); if the evidence shows the contract was violated, the affected work is quarantined (③) and either re-checked and re-admitted (④) or explained to the person, who decides what happens next (⑤).

steps.d: safety, intent, correctness and organizational rules, stated at the level people reason about
what each agent, guardrail and hand-off may assume and must guarantee
checked assembly of agent teams and the state they share
does the composed team still meet its concerns?
transcripts, tool calls and executions, abundant but unreadable at scale
which agent handed what to whom, and which version, approval and context produced a behaviour
the few components whose interaction explains a symptom
why an objective was or was not achieved, in terms people can check

tip.d: When a lesson, skill or hand-off turns out to be wrong, everything recorded as exposed to it is suspended in every deployment
Suspended items return only after a fresh check, as new versions, and only a bounded number of times
The responsible person sees exactly what was affected and why, and decides what changes in the contract

cards.body: Concerns such as safety, intent and organizational rules usually reach an agent as prose. I turn them into foundational contracts: models of what each agent, guardrail and hand-off may assume and must guarantee, composed and checked before the team runs.

Transcripts and tool logs are abundant but unreadable at scale. I record hand-offs and provenance while agents work, and abstract them into slices and explanations, so a person can see which agent produced what, from which evidence, and why an objective was or was not met.

When a learned lesson, a skill or a hand-off turns out to be wrong, deleting it is not enough: its effects have already spread into other artifacts and deployments. Recorded lineage finds everything it touched and suspends it everywhere. It is re-admitted only after a fresh check, a bounded number of times, and otherwise explained to the person responsible.

cards.h3: One object, checked in both directions
cards.body: Specifications without evidence cannot tell us whether they were honored; evidence without specifications gives us nothing to check against. A foundational contract holds both. This figure follows its own rule: it is generated from a state-machine model, and on every build a model checker verifies that a person can always be reached and that every violation is contained and ends with a person.
